body.x: OTITON MEDICAL CO., LTD. (CEO Jayden JAEYOUNG KIM) participated in the Global Media Online Meet-Up on July 3, co-hosted with U.S. tech media Ubergizmo, targeting Korean startups.
The event, organized by AVING News and Ubergizmo, focuses on introducing Korean products and technologies to the global market, particularly those applying for the CES 2026 Innovation Awards.

Founded in 2022, OTITON Medical is a healthcare tech company aiming to make diagnosis and care for inner ear conditions accessible from home. CEO Jayden Kim, an electronics engineering expert with over 17 years of hardware design experience, has been directly involved in developing smart thermometers and therapy devices.

Its flagship brand, ‘Doctor In Home’, provides personalized health management and AI-assisted diagnostics via AI and IoT-based smart medical devices. Users can monitor their health from home and track data systematically.

Starting October 2024, OTITON officially showcased its first product, a smart thermometer, at global exhibitions such as MWC Las Vegas/Barcelona, BIO Japan, HLTH Las Vegas, and AUS BIO Australia. The product received a CES 2025 Innovation Award, validating its technical and market potential.

body.cap: Jayden JAEYOUNG KIM of OTITON Medical takes questions during the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Thursday, July 3 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: OTITON also participated in GMEP and NEXTRISE expos, forming connections with buyers. It is in active partnership talks with companies in Türkiye and Singapore and is currently testing products with Australia’s In Vitro Technologies for distribution in Australia and New Zealand.

Its CES 2025 award-winning smart thermometer features an endoscopic camera and high-precision sensor, enabling early home diagnosis of ear infections. It includes AI-powered analysis and mobile app integration for enhanced usability and accuracy.

The award boosted OTITON’s brand recognition in global markets such as the U.S., Japan, China, Australia, and Vietnam, and led to increased interest from overseas hospitals and distributors. It also expanded opportunities for partnerships, collaborations, and investment, and served as a major milestone for Doctor In Home’s global expansion.

For CES 2026, OTITON will again compete with a new lineup of smart devices combining precision medical and AI technology. The first one is a smart therapy device for humans that combines endoscopic imaging and infrared sensors to monitor and treat inflammation and injuries inside the ear in real-time. The second one is a smart thermometer for pets equipped with clinical-grade algorithms and high-sensitivity temperature sensors. The last one is a smart therapy device for pets that visualizes problem areas using an endoscopic camera and delivers infrared heat treatment.

body.cap: Smart thermometer for pets (left) and smart therapy device head part for pets (right) | Image provided by OTITON Medical

body.x: All three products feature intuitive, portable curved form factors with soft colors. Pet devices are designed with skin-friendly materials and minimal noise to reduce stress. The user interface is optimized with one-button operation and LCD feedback, ensuring accessibility for seniors and first-time users.

The core innovation is compressing high-spec hospital-grade equipment into consumer-friendly home devices. These hybrid devices combine endoscopy and heat therapy and are integrated with a cloud-based smartphone monitoring system—a rare approach in the pet healthcare market.

The products address global challenges such as limited medical infrastructure, aging populations, and the growing pet-care trend. OTITON’s solutions enable early, safe treatment from home using 650nm infrared lamps, helping to close the gap in veterinary care access.

To scale globally, OTITON is executing a strategic expansion plan. It will participate in exhibitions in Germany and Jakarta this September to raise brand awareness and expand partnerships in Europe and Southeast Asia. A legal entity is being established in Shibuya, Japan, to strengthen distribution and localize strategies across Asia.

body.cap: Harim Jang of OTITON Medical pitches at the Global Media Meet-Up held at MIK Base Camp in Seocho-gu, Seoul, on Thursday, July 3 | Photo by AVING News

body.x: In 2026, OTITON plans to continue attending major global exhibitions like CES to showcase its smart healthcare technologies and expand distribution partnerships in key markets such as the U.S., Australia, and Singapore.

The U.S., as the world’s largest digital healthcare market with strong demand for telemedicine and home medical devices, offers high potential for Doctor In Home. Local buyer interest in OTITON increased significantly after its CES 2025 award.

The company has also laid the groundwork in Japan through its selection as a Shibuya startup and participation in BIO JAPAN. Product testing with In Vitro Technologies is underway in Australia, with expansion planned across Oceania. Singapore and Türkiye, where connections were formed through GMEP and NEXTRISE, are also viewed as strategic markets due to their developed and emerging healthcare infrastructures.

“Our goal is to spread AI TECH-based healthcare solutions globally, starting with Korea and Japan,” said an OTITON Medical representative. “We are developing tailored strategies for each country’s medical regulations and distribution structures, and aim to introduce our tech-driven solutions to the world through global partnerships.”

body.x: Founded in 2005, Ubergizmo operates the Silicon Valley Post and publishes content in six languages across 200 countries, with a focus on electronics and technology. It regularly covers major global exhibitions such as CES, IFA, and MWC. Ubergizmo co-founder and CTO Hubert Nguyen attended the event. He previously worked as an NVIDIA programming engineer, developer education program manager, and 3D graphics programmer. He covers products and technologies from around the world at CES each year.
